cohort: The study included 130 antenatal subjects with premature rupture of membranes (PROM) admitted to the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, NSCB Medical College.
finding: The study found that induction of labor in pregnancies complicated by PROM resulted in a mean induction-to-delivery time of 11+/-3.42 hours and was associated with a higher rate of vaginal deliveries compared to non-induced cases.
mod_finding: Among induced cases, 64% had a vaginal delivery, while 36% underwent LSCS, and a significantly higher proportion of subjects who were not induced delivered via LSCS (72.7%, p<0.05).
